meta.title: SNAP Eligibility Changes Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025
meta.description: Timeline of implementation events affecting SNAP (food assistance) eligibility by state, beginning with enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on July 4, 2025. Focused on work requirement expansion and noncitizen eligibility restrictions.

timeline.monthLabel: July 4, 2025 — One Big Beautiful Bill signed

updates.description: Work requirement age for able-bodied adults without dependents raised to 18 through 64 years old, previously 18 through 54. Parents whose youngest child is 14 or older are now subject to the three-month time limit. Effective immediately upon enactment in all states.

Refugees, people granted asylum, trafficking survivors, and certain humanitarian parolees lose federal food assistance eligibility immediately. Only lawful permanent residents, Cuban-Haitian entrants, and Compacts of Free Association migrants remain eligible as noncitizens.

States begin mailing written notices to households newly subject to the work time limit, specifically adults ages 55 through 64 and parents whose youngest child is 14 through 17. Recipients have until October 31 to submit exemption verification or face enforcement beginning November 1.

source.label: FNS Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Exceptions Implementation Memo, Oct. 3, 2025

timeline.monthLabel: October 2025 — Noncitizen eligibility grace period ends

updates.description: Federal guidance issued October 31 confirms noncitizen eligibility changes take full effect November 1, 2025. States begin removing newly ineligible noncitizens from food assistance rolls at their next recertification appointment.

source.label: FNS Alien Eligibility Implementation Memo, Oct. 31, 2025

updates.description: States begin counting November as the first month toward the three-month benefit time limit for newly covered adults, those ages 55 through 64 and parents of teenagers. Federal quality control error tracking begins for states that incorrectly pay benefits to people now subject to the time limit.

source.label: FNS Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Waivers Implementation Memo, Oct. 3, 2025

updates.description: Most states begin screening all food assistance recipients against the new work requirement rules at their next scheduled recertification. New applicants are screened immediately upon application. States that previously held geographic waivers face a contested November 2 waiver termination.

source.label: Propel, Full Guide to Work Requirements in 2026

timeline.monthLabel: January 2026 — First benefit losses from work time limit

updates.description: The first wave of recipients who accumulated three countable months under the new work time limit rules begin losing food assistance eligibility. An estimated 750,000 people nationally face benefit termination in early 2026, concentrated in states without court-ordered protections.

source.label: No Kid Hungry, Summary of SNAP Changes in HR1

timeline.monthLabel: February 2026 — Work time limits begin in waiver-protected states

updates.category: Work time limit enforcement begins in waiver-protected states
updates.description: States that previously held geographic waivers exempting large portions of their population from the work time limit begin enforcement as those protections expire. Adults ages 18 through 64 who are not exempt begin accumulating months toward the three-month time limit. California and Washington, which have among the highest shares of food assistance recipients subject to the new rules, begin mailing enforcement notices.

source.label: Food and Nutrition Administration, ABAWD Waivers Implementation Memo

timeline.monthLabel: March 1, 2026 — New York work requirements take effect

updates.category: Work time limit enforcement begins in New York
updates.description: New York begins enforcing the expanded work time limit on March 1, 2026, one of the last states to implement the new rules after exhausting available implementation extensions. Able-bodied adults without dependents ages 18 through 64 in New York City and statewide must now document 80 hours per month of work, job training, or approved volunteer activity or face benefit termination after three months.

source.label: Food and Nutrition Administration, ABAWD Waivers Implementation Memo

timeline.monthLabel: April 2026 — Noncitizen eligibility cuts take effect in court-protected states

updates.category: Noncitizen eligibility cuts reach previously protected states
updates.description: Court orders that temporarily shielded refugees, people granted asylum, and certain humanitarian parolees from food assistance eligibility cuts in sixteen states expire or are lifted. States begin removing newly ineligible noncitizens from food assistance rolls at their next recertification appointment, completing the nationwide implementation of the noncitizen eligibility restrictions enacted July 4, 2025.

source.label: Food and Nutrition Administration, Alien Eligibility Implementation Memo

timeline.monthLabel: June 2026 — Work requirement benefit terminations reach waiver states

updates.category: Benefit terminations begin in formerly waiver-protected states
updates.description: Recipients in states that began enforcement in February and March 2026 who have now accumulated three countable months under the work time limit begin losing food assistance eligibility. California, New York, and Washington see the largest absolute numbers of terminations among this group, as their populations subject to the new rules are significantly larger than in states that implemented earlier.

source.label: Food and Nutrition Administration, SNAP Work Requirements
